\chapter{Build and Height}
\label{ch:ml-build}
\hlchaptermodality{101}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can describe a person as short, thin or stout, and say that someone is tall.}

From cold: three adjectives that go in front of the noun, and one noun that cannot.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[kuṟiya]{\ml{കുറിയ} (kuṟiya) — short, of a person}

\label{lesson:ML-C101-kuriya}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{small}. Then say \emph{he}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} — \emph{kuṟiya} — \textbf{short}, said of a person's height.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{അവൻ} \ml{കുറിയ} \ml{കുട്ടിയാണ്}.} — \emph{avan kuṟiya kuṭṭiyāṇŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}He is a short child.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Put it beside the word you already have and the shape is the same.}

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{romanized} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{ചെറിയ}} & \emph{ceṟiya} \\
\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} & \emph{kuṟiya} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Same \textbf{\ml{റ}}, same \textbf{-\ml{ിയ}} ending, same job in the sentence: in front of the noun, unchanged, exactly as the adjective chapter said.

\textbf{What differs is the meaning, not the shape.} \textbf{\ml{ചെറിയ}} is \emph{small} — little, not much of it. \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} is \emph{short} — not long, and of a person, not tall. A child can be \textbf{\ml{ചെറിയ}} and a child can be \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}}, and those say two different things about the child.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kuṟiya}
  \item \emph{ceṟiya}, then \emph{kuṟiya}, and hear how little separates them
  \item \emph{avan kuṟiya kuṭṭiyāṇŭ}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{short}, of a person? (\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}}.) Which word you already had is built the same way? (\textbf{\ml{ചെറിയ}}.) And where does it stand? (\textbf{In front of the noun, unchanged}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[meliñña]{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ} (meliñña) — thin}

\label{lesson:ML-C101-melinja}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{short}, of a person. Where does it stand?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ}} — \emph{meliñña} — \textbf{thin}, said of a person's build.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ} \ml{കുട്ടി}} — \emph{meliñña kuṭṭi} — \textquotedblleft{}a thin child.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{The ending is the constant; the shape in front of it never was.}

\textbf{\ml{വലിയ}}, \textbf{\ml{നല്ല}}, \textbf{\ml{പുതിയ}}, \textbf{\ml{പഴയ}}, \textbf{\ml{ചെറിയ}}, and now \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} — every adjective the book has put in front of a noun ends in \textbf{-a}, and so does this one. That is the whole requirement, and \textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ}} meets it.

What comes in front of the \textbf{-a} has never been fixed. \textbf{\ml{വലിയ}}, \textbf{\ml{പുതിയ}}, \textbf{\ml{ചെറിയ}} and \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} end \textbf{-\ml{ിയ}}, but \textbf{\ml{നല്ല}} ends \textbf{-\ml{ല്ല}} and \textbf{\ml{പഴയ}} ends in a plain \textbf{-\ml{യ}}. \textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ}} adds a doubled \textbf{\ml{ഞ്ഞ}} to that list — a shape you have had since \textbf{\ml{പച്ച}} and \textbf{\ml{മഞ്ഞ}}, back among the colours.

\textbf{That changes nothing about how it is used} — it still stands before the noun and still does not change:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ} \ml{കുട്ടി}} & \emph{kuṟiya kuṭṭi} \\
\textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ} \ml{കുട്ടി}} & \emph{meliñña kuṭṭi} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{meliñña}
  \item \emph{meliñña kuṭṭi}
  \item \emph{kuṟiya kuṭṭi}, then \emph{meliñña kuṭṭi}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{thin}? (\textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ}}.) What do all the adjectives so far end in? (\textbf{-a}.) Does this one behave any differently? (\textbf{No} — in front, unchanged.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[taṭicca]{\ml{തടിച്ച} (taṭicca) — stout}

\label{lesson:ML-C101-thadicha}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{a thin child}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{തടിച്ച}} — \emph{taṭicca} — \textbf{stout}, \textbf{heavily built}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{തടിച്ച} \ml{കുട്ടി}} — \emph{taṭicca kuṭṭi} — \textquotedblleft{}a stout child.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{This is the far end of the last word}, and the book has done that before: one quality, then its opposite, so a single axis costs you two words and not four.

Three shapes, one ending, one behaviour:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{adjective} & \textbf{ends} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} & \textbf{-\ml{ിയ}} \\
\textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ}} & \textbf{-\ml{ഞ്ഞ}} \\
\textbf{\ml{തടിച്ച}} & \textbf{-\ml{ച്ച}} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Every one of them closes on \textbf{-a}, stands in front of the noun, and does not change. \textbf{The shape in front of the -a varies and never matters} — as \textbf{\ml{നല്ല}} and \textbf{\ml{പഴയ}} were already showing you before this chapter began.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{taṭicca}
  \item \emph{meliñña kuṭṭi}, then \emph{taṭicca kuṭṭi}
  \item all three adjectives from this chapter in a row
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{stout}? (\textbf{\ml{തടിച്ച}}.) And its opposite? (\textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ}}.) What do the three shapes of this chapter have in common? (\textbf{They all end in -a and none of them changes}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[uyaraṁ]{\ml{ഉയരം} (uyaraṁ) — height}

\label{lesson:ML-C101-uyaram}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{short}, of a person. Then say the word for \emph{there is}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{ഉയരം}} — \emph{uyaraṁ} — \textbf{height.}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ഉയരമുണ്ട്}.} — \emph{enikkŭ uyaramuṇṭŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}To me, height exists\textquotedblright{} — I am tall.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{There is no single word for \emph{tall} in this book, and this is how you say it anyway.}

\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} was an adjective, so it went in front of a noun. \textbf{\ml{ഉയരം}} is not an adjective — it is a \textbf{noun}, \emph{height} — so it takes the other machine you already own: the one where a thing \textbf{exists to someone}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ഉയരമുണ്ട്}.} — \emph{enikkŭ uyaramuṇṭŭ} — to-me height there-is — \emph{I am tall.}
\end{quote}

\textbf{That frame is not new.} The chapter that gave you \textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ട്}} used it to say that someone \emph{has} a thing, and the chapter on \textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്}} gave you the person the having happens to. All this chapter does is put a new noun into it.

And the \textbf{\ml{ം}} does here what it does \textbf{before \ml{ആണ്}} — it takes the full letter \textbf{\ml{മ}} so it can carry what follows: \textbf{\ml{ഉയരം}} + \textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ട്}} $\to$ \textbf{\ml{ഉയരമുണ്ട്}}.

\textbf{Do not read that as a rule about every ending.} The chapter on easy and hard told you the \textbf{\ml{ം}} does different things for different endings, and this chapter's own title proves it: \textbf{\ml{ഉയരം}} + \textbf{\ml{ഉം}} is \textbf{\ml{ഉയരവും}}, with a \textbf{\ml{വ}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{uyaraṁ}
  \item \emph{enikkŭ uyaramuṇṭŭ}
  \item why this one needs \textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ട്}} and \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} did not
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{height}? (\textbf{\ml{ഉയരം}}.) How do you say \emph{I am tall}? (\textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ഉയരമുണ്ട്}}.) And why not an adjective, as with \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}}? (\textbf{Because \ml{ഉയരം} is a noun} — it exists to someone.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[uyaravuṁ kuṟiyayuṁ enna ōrmma]{(short, thin, stout, and height) — from cold}

\label{lesson:ML-R101-build-recall}



\begin{quote}
Close the lessons before this one. Say \emph{short}, \emph{thin}, \emph{stout}, and \emph{height}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: three of them go in front, and one cannot}]
Three of this chapter's four words are \textbf{adjectives}, and all three behave the way every adjective in the book has:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{adjective} & \textbf{before the noun} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} & \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ} \ml{കുട്ടി}} (\emph{kuṟiya kuṭṭi}) \\
\textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ}} & \textbf{\ml{മെലിഞ്ഞ} \ml{കുട്ടി}} (\emph{meliñña kuṭṭi}) \\
\textbf{\ml{തടിച്ച}} & \textbf{\ml{തടിച്ച} \ml{കുട്ടി}} (\emph{taṭicca kuṭṭi}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

They end \textbf{-\ml{ിയ}}, \textbf{-\ml{ഞ്ഞ}} and \textbf{-\ml{ച്ച}} — three different shapes, all closing on \textbf{-a}, none of them changing for the noun behind it.

\textbf{\ml{ഉയരം} is the odd one, and not because it is irregular.} It is a \textbf{noun}, so there is nothing for it to stand in front of. It uses the frame you were given for \emph{having}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ഉയരമുണ്ട്}.} — \emph{enikkŭ uyaramuṇṭŭ} — to-me height there-is — \emph{I am tall.}
\end{quote}
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
\textbf{The book still has no single word for \emph{tall}.} It has a noun for height and a way to say that someone has it, and between them that is the whole meaning.

That is worth noticing rather than papering over: \textbf{\ml{ചെറിയ}} and \textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}} are almost the same word and do not mean the same thing — one is \emph{small}, the other \emph{short} — and \emph{tall} is the mirror of neither. You reach it by another route.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kuṟiya}, \emph{meliñña}, \emph{taṭicca}, \emph{uyaraṁ}
  \item \emph{taṭicca kuṭṭi}, then \emph{meliñña kuṭṭi}
  \item \emph{enikkŭ uyaramuṇṭŭ}
  \item which of the four cannot stand in front of a noun, and why
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Short, stout, height? (\textbf{\ml{കുറിയ}, \ml{തടിച്ച}, \ml{ഉയരം}}.) Which of the three cannot go in front of a noun? (\textbf{\ml{ഉയരം}} — it is a noun itself.) So how do you say \emph{I am tall}? (\textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ഉയരമുണ്ട്}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
